precepts.text: A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will. For every solution, these people got five excuses.
precepts.point: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me. Churches don't read that; churches will look at that and go, no, we're not reading that in Sunday school. You know what it means further? You ain't going to just be able to do what you want to do. You was put on this earth to do what the Most High and Christ said, and if you don't do that, then there's no reason for you to live. He said, if you don't want to do what you were created for, bring him before me and end his existence.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
The third servant came with excuses: “Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin: For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man.” And the Lord answered, “Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant.”

“A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” For every solution, these people have five excuses. The wicked servant would not own that he did nothing with what he was given; he blamed his lord for being austere.

Your excuses are not going to fly with Christ. He doesn't care about your excuses. He knew exactly what the servant knew: “Thou knewest that I was an austere man, taking up that I laid not down, and reaping that I did not sow.” If you knew it, you should have done something with it.

precepts.text: Do nothing without advice, and when thou hast once done, repent not.
precepts.point: No brothers counsel the women: senior sisters deal with the sisters and bring matters to leadership when they need judgment; that is the protocol.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

precepts.why:
“Do nothing without advice; and when thou hast once done, repent not.” The ones who watch for your souls give the counsel, and you are not to move without it. Sisters, you have been given the blueprint, the things to look for when it comes to men.

When looking for a husband, you are trying to identify stability and discipline. “He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.” He is not stable; how is he going to take care of you? He is blown about with every wind of doctrine, bringing out little dumb breakdowns that did not come from leadership, like mashed potatoes on the Passover. Red flag. “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways”: one minute it’s this, the next minute it’s that. Spiritually you should never aim down; aim up for a man with more understanding than you, who can lead and guide you. If you marry a novice and you are the one teaching him to wear fringes every day, you lose respect for him, and you have married down. And don’t think you are going to change him; men typically do not look to you for counsel.

“But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” A brother barely able to feed himself, getting kicked out of apartments, lights cut off, staying at his cousin’s house, is not ready for a wife, and you are not stepping in to save a negro. Spot the signs of lust: a brother telling you at 11 p.m. that he is naked is setting the mood and lining you up. Get the hell off the phone and put him in his place. And ask leadership how he handles correction: “he that hateth reproof is brutish”, and a man who cannot take correction from the men over him has a problem with God.

If you see these signs early, congratulations, sister, you spotted him. Now are you going to play dumb because you like the idea of being married, or wise up and follow counsel? Do nothing without advice, and once you have done it with advice, you will not have to repent of it. Break the cycle.

precepts.text: A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will. Do not hear a class like this and say that ain't it; that is the excuse to go back to your pleasure. Sirach 6:4, a wicked soul shall destroy him that hath it and make him laughed to scorn of his enemies. Sirach 27:3, unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.
precepts.point: Romans 6:16-19: to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are. Fall into sin and you worship the devil in that moment; you cannot serve two masters. As ye yielded your members to uncleanness, now yield them to righteousness unto holiness. Satan says you fell and cannot get up; you can repent, that is why Christ came.
precepts.why:
“A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” When you hear a class like this, do not say, Oh, that ain’t it. You are just making an excuse to go back to your pleasure and your lust, to feel comfortable in them.

The excuse maker starts a fight over the chicken so he can leave and get some duck. It is like the story the Bishop told about the co-worker who dealt with multiple women and would start a fight with one to go see the other. Now you are pointing the finger at everybody else, when back at the ranch you really want to go have fun in your pleasure and your lust. As the Bishop’s graphic says, a sin-filled soul will find and make excuses only to fulfill its lust. That is very dangerous.

“A wicked soul shall destroy him that hath it, and shall make him to be laughed to scorn of his enemies.” And “Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.”

So we have to have fear and we have to be diligent if we want a fighting chance. The man hasty in his words, who always has an excuse ready, will not be reproved, and that is why there is more hope of a fool than of him.

precepts.text: He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment.
precepts.point: Verse 3 says meats are received with thanksgiving by them which believe and know the truth. The truth is the law, so the meat is sanctified by the word, not by a prayer over it.
precepts.why:
Paul says the meats are received “of them which believe and know the truth.” What is it to believe? “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment”. If you take heed to the commandments, you believe. Does a Christian believe in the commandments? So when he says you can eat anything as long as you receive it with thanksgiving, no: you can pray all you want, but you don't believe and you don't know the truth. Those are the very things that can save your life.

Finish the verse: “and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” If you believe in the commandments and keep the dietary laws, will you be worrying about high blood pressure? Will you be worrying about a foot amputation because of diabetes, about high cholesterol, about gout that takes brothers' fingers and feet? No, because you are not eating in a way where those sicknesses can come your way. The law tells you the food you can eat and the food you cannot eat.

All of that comes because people wanted to eat nasty, dirty food the Lord said don't eat. So take heed to yourself. Believing is not a prayer said over the plate; it is taking heed to the commandment, and the one who does fares never the worse.

precepts.text: Once the judgment is done, the apology does not undo it; the counsel had to be taken beforehand.
precepts.point: They returned and wept before the Lord, but the Lord would not hearken to their voice nor give ear. When counsel is set at nought until the judgment lands, the weeping comes too late; they that hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord seek him early and do not find him. So they abode in Kadesh many days.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

precepts.why:
“Do nothing without advice; and when thou hast once done, repent not.” The advice was there the whole time: dread not, neither be afraid, the Lord your God shall fight for you. Israel would not take it, and the Lord sware that generation would not see the land. Only after the judgment fell did they want to repent, girding on every man his weapons of war and declaring themselves ready to go up.

Once the judgment is done, the apology does not undo it. “We have sinned against the Lord” and weeping before the Lord did not reverse what was sworn; the counsel had to be taken beforehand. Then they acted without advice a second time, going up when the Lord said go not up, and were chased as bees and destroyed unto Hormah. The counsel comes before the doing, and when the thing is once done, there is no repenting it back.

precepts.text: He that believeth in the Most High taketh heed to the commandments, tying true belief to obedience.
precepts.point: They caused their sons and daughters to pass through the fire, used divinations and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil.

note.label: 2 Kings 17: The Carrying Away of Israel

precepts.why:
“He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment; and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.”

True belief is tied to obedience. Israel hardened their necks “like to the neck of their fathers, that did not believe in the Lord their God”, and the proof they did not believe is that they rejected his statutes and his covenant.

To believe in the Most High is to take heed to the commandments. Those who claim belief while breaking the commandments do not truly believe.

precepts.text: They that fear the Lord shall find judgment and kindle justice as a light.
precepts.point: He cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall He judge the world and the people with equity. Righteousness means us keeping God's commandments, observing and doing them, and equity means justice, the practice of giving what is due. By His righteousness He is going to give the people the justice due to them.

note.label: Psalm 98: Sing Unto the Lord a New Song

precepts.why:
He shall judge the people with equity. Equity means justice, the practice of giving what is due. “They that fear the Lord shall find judgment, and shall kindle justice as a light.”

Those that fear the Lord find judgment and kindle justice as a light. By his righteousness he is going to give the people the justice due to them.

precepts.text: He that believes in the Lord takes heed to the commandment and shall fare never the worse; that is how you receive the equity, the justice, due to you.
precepts.point: He cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall He judge the world and the people with equity. Righteousness means us keeping God's commandments, observing and doing them, and equity means justice, the practice of giving what is due. By His righteousness He is going to give the people the justice due to them.

note.label: Psalm 98: Sing Unto the Lord a New Song

precepts.why:
“He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment; and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” Believing in the Lord is taking heed to the commandment, and he that trusts in him shall fare never the worse.

That is how you receive the equity, the justice due to you, when he comes to judge the people: by keeping his commandments, which is the righteousness he judges by.

precepts.text: Use few words, especially among great men.
precepts.point: Let thy speech be short, comprehending much in few words; speak only when there is need of thee and hold thy tongue among great men.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“He that hath knowledge spareth his words: and a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit. Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise.” Talking too much, especially without the words of the Most High, marks a fool.

“Speak, young man, if there be need of thee: and yet scarcely when thou art twice asked.” Speak only when there is need of thee, and hold thy tongue among great men. Let thy speech be short, comprehending much in few words.
This is what the servant with the napkin is doing. “A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” Them old excuse makers.

points: He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment. That is what belief means. Belief makes you take heed to God's commandments. The black church has not figured that one out yet; most of them do not even know about the Apocrypha.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

points: There take thy pastime, and do what thou wilt: but sin not by proud speech. You can have your fun on this earth, but God listens to your speech. For all these things bless him that made thee: always remember you have a creator; do not turn into a hater.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: Whoso feareth the Lord will receive his discipline. God is correcting us right now: the president is in a position to make our lives miserable because we are being corrected by God. It is important to see this as discipline from God. And they that seek him early shall find favour: do not wait until the whole world is falling apart to seek God.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: He that seeketh the law shall be filled therewith: that is why we teach you to follow God's laws, and the denominations call us legalists. But the hypocrite will be offended thereat. They that fear the Lord shall find judgment, and shall kindle justice as a light: we cannot bring forth justice on our own; we do not need bombs or a military; all we need is to be filled with the law. Fringes, skirts and head coverings, beards, the Sabbath: you are not doing anything evil, but it bothers people.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will. There is nothing you can tell them; in their heart they believe they can sin and win. It is the same in the congregation and in your house: you show them every scripture and they give you every excuse. After a while, do not chase them, replace them.
